report.summary: The panel now reaches the household broker over TLS at mqtts://homeassistant.gdenu.fi:8123 (used as the default when none is saved), with the certificate name check skipped because the valid certificate is issued for a different host — the chain is still verified and an optional CA can be pinned. Builds at 2.93 MB, 20 % free.
decisions: Used the narrowest switch that satisfies the constraint: skip_cert_common_name_check on a TLS session. The certificate chain is still verified against the built-in pack (or a CA supplied at runtime), so encryption and server authentication stay on; only the hostname match — which can never succeed for this box — is skipped.
The rule applies to every TLS URI (mqtts://, ssl://, mqtt:// on 8883), so editing the broker later keeps the same behaviour; plain mqtt:// is untouched.

Default broker is now mqtts://homeassistant.gdenu.fi:8123 when nothing is stored, so a freshly flashed panel needs only Wi-Fi to reach the household broker; the settings page and its TLS hint carry the same default.

Added an optional runtime CA (app_mqtt_set_broker_ca) so a household that later wants strict chain pinning can supply it from the settings page; with no CA the ESP-IDF certificate pack authenticates the chain.
report.build: esp32s31 success — 0x2cc2d0 (2933456 B) in a 0x380000 partition, 20% free; check_code clean
openQuestions: Home Assistant's add-on terminates TLS for its own web UI on 8123; whether the Mosquitto add-on also accepts MQTT-over-TLS on that same port is a server-side fact I cannot verify from here. If it does not, point the broker URI at whatever port the household's broker really listens on (still mqtts://) — the code path does not change.
Broker username/password (and the optional CA PEM) are still entered on the settings page apart from the URI; no credential is baked into the firmware.
